A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HybridNorm work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original dense and MoE training results, downstream evaluations, normalization ablations, and scaling and depth experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds a 200B-token comparison and layerwise signal-propagation and entropy analyses.

M1.justification: The HybridNorm equations, QKV normalization, FFN normalization, and specialized first-block variant are unchanged. V1 Equations (8)–(11) match v3 Equations (6)–(7), and Algorithm 1 retains the same procedure.

E1.justification: OLMoE Mix pretraining, downstream tasks, and appendix validation corpora are retained. The added comparisons and internal-model diagnostics do not introduce a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: V3 Table 8 expands the 1.2B comparison to include Post-Norm and Mix-LN, previously evaluated only in smaller-model comparisons. Table 4's extra QK-norm row redisplays the existing Pre-QK-Pre configuration rather than introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: V3 adds a 200B-token evaluation of 1.2B models alongside the retained 1T-token comparison. New diagnostics track token cosine similarity and layerwise entropy across training steps. Existing model configurations and stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D.2–D.3 add substantial analyses of representation degeneration and entropy dynamics, comparing four normalization methods across 16 layers in Figures 7–8. The existing initialization, normalization-position, first-block, gradient, scaling, and depth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3's added results retain the existing point-estimate and training-curve reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained, but Table 8 adds a five-method comparison at 200B tokens: HybridNorm* averages 60.67, Pre-Norm 59.56, and HybridNorm 59.18. Figures 7–8 additionally report token-similarity and entropy findings. These are added results, not improvements over the retained 1T-token scores.

T1.justification: V3 extends the existing theory with hybrid-block Jacobians, a Pre-Norm-plus-QK-Norm lemma and proof, and proofs of supporting norm bounds. Theorem 2 revises dimensional factors and changes minimum-singular-value definitions from XW to W. Its proof also changes ||X_N||_F from sqrt(sd) to sqrt(s), despite retaining the RMSNorm definition.

C1.justification: The central HybridNorm contribution and superiority claims remain. V3 explicitly promotes theoretical support in the abstract, contributions, and conclusion, while dropping v1's broader state-of-the-art assertion from the abstract.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations involving three-way gradient coupling, representation degeneration, and entropy stability. Appendix D.1 attributes Post-Norm's weaker results to untuned default hyperparameters. Appendix G.2 explicitly limits larger-model extrapolation and distinguishes gradient stability from guaranteed performance; the MoE discussion also acknowledges task-specific underperformance.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses A100-80GB hardware, 32/64-GPU allocations, one-to-ten-day pretraining durations, and the absence of extensive hyperparameter search. Existing hyperparameters, pseudocode, and project link remain. V1's direct OLMoE Mix URL and explicit 0.8-EMA caption note are omitted.

R1.justification: V3 expands positioning through Sandwich-LN, Gemma 2, vision-transformer normalization, and OLMo-2's normalization placement, with additional citations supporting entropy and mathematical analyses. It extends the Mix-LN comparison with layer-uniformity and post-training arguments. The original positioning and QKV-Norm attribution remain.

P1.justification: V3 separates preliminaries, HybridNorm, and theoretical analysis; combines dense and MoE results under one section; moves related work into the appendix; and reorganizes proofs, implementation details, and supplementary results. It adds a contents page and rewrites explanatory passages, although much experimental prose remains.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column branded report with a redesigned title and abstract. Existing plots are rearranged and resized, and Tables 3–4 are restructured. Table 8, two layerwise diagnostic figures, and the unified normalization diagram are added; the original appendix benchmark plots are retained as Figures 9–10.

improvement.justification: The added comparator experiment, diagnostics, hardware disclosures, and explicit limitations strengthen empirical assessment and transparency. However, v3 Appendix B.4 replaces v1's correct RMSNorm identity ||X_N||_F = sqrt(sd) with sqrt(s), contradicting the retained definition and affecting the revised bounds. This unresolved inconsistency in a newly emphasized theoretical contribution makes the net quality effect uncertain despite the empirical and documentation gains.
